question: Which of the following states had the least decadal growth in literacy rate, as per census 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mizoram recorded the **least decadal growth** in literacy rate among Indian states as per the Census 2011.
 
• The literacy rate in Mizoram increased from **88.8%** in 2001 to **91.6%** in 2011, marking a growth of **2.8%**.
 
• In contrast, other states such as Tripura and Kerala showed higher decadal growth rates in literacy.
 
• Mizoram's high base literacy rate in 2001 contributed to the smaller percentage increase over the decade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate Definition:**

 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011:**
 
 
• The Census 2011 is the 15th National Census survey conducted by the Government of India.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters including literacy rates.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Literacy:**
 
 
• Kerala had the highest literacy rate in India as per Census 2011, with a literacy rate of 94%.
 
• Kerala's focused educational policies have historically contributed to its high literacy rates.
 
 
 
• **Tripura's Literacy Growth:**
 
 
• Tripura saw a significant increase in its literacy rate, from 73.2% in 2001 to 87.2% in 2011, marking a growth of 14%.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Higher literacy rates contribute to economic growth, poverty reduction, and improved health outcomes.
 
• Literacy empowers individuals and enhances their ability to participate fully in societal activities.
